Highest-frequency design-system violation | 346 | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | 347 | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | 348 | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | 349 | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | 350 351 Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. 352 353 ### Gate zero — does it actually build? 354 355 **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this 356 project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously 357 supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part 358 of your day. 359 360 ```bash 361 npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean 362 npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise 363 npx vitest run 364 ``` 365 366 Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: 367 368 - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the 369 same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It 370 typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. 371 - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo 372 rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Check whether the 373 rule or the code is wrong before raising it as a code finding. 374 375 Make "green locally before opening" the expectation, and say so once to the whole team rather than 376 per-PR. It isn't about blame — it's that the review budget is an hour per PR and this spends it on nothing. 377 378 ### Review across three surfaces, not one 379 380 Reading the diff is the smallest part. For any UI PR, look at all three: 381 382 | Surface | What only it will tell you | 383 |---|---| 384 | **The diff** | Tokens vs literals, reuse vs reimplementation, abstractions respected | 385 | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — states, responsive behaviour, whether hover/focus work at all | 386 | **Figma** | Whether the rendered output matches the design, and which gaps are design gaps rather than build gaps | 387 388 Every `feature/*` and `fix/*` branch now auto-deploys to its own MRT environment and posts the URL on the 389 PR. There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put 390 it beside Figma.** If no URL comment appeared, the branch had no open PR when it was pushed; a further 391 push once the PR exists will post it. 392 393 Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything 394 that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, 395 not the developer's. 396 397 ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check 398 399 This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have 400 drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. 401 402 `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 403 404 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 405 2. Semantic token strings — `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"` 406 3. The component's own `theme/components/.ts` for variant / size / state 407 4. `sx` only for a genuine prop-system gap 408 5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly can't express it 409 410 What to actively look for: 411 412 - **The correct token, not just a token.** A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token 413 passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves. Two `sx` blocks recently 414 hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. 415 - **`var(--zimm-*)` in the right layer.** It is the convention *inside* `theme/components/*.ts`. In 416 component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer. 417 - **`--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** They exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes. The 418 named scale (`m`, `l`, `xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface. 419 - **A theme recipe that nothing consumes.** A `theme/components/.ts` file that is written and 420 registered but never read via `useStyleConfig` looks like compliance and is dead code. 421 - **A second copy of the token registry.** Any new utility that re-types token names as strings 422 reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed. 423 - **Interaction states in JavaScript.** `useState` for hover / press / focus instead of 424 `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible` means those states are dead until hydration, sticky on touch, 425 and unreachable by the theme. 426 427 ### Tests and stories — the minimum, while UI is the focus 428 429 The build focus is UI, and that's fine — but don't let coverage reach zero on the way through: 430 431 - **Unit tests where they earn their place** — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. Not for 432 re-exports or passthroughs. 433 - **At minimum, scaffold the Storybook story.** Every component exported from its folder needs one. A 434 scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states is the floor, even if the `play` 435 function comes later. It's also the surface your own review depends on. 436 437 ### Review questions, in order 438 439 0. **Does it build?** `tsc`, lint, tests — gate zero above 440 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 441 2. **Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?** 442 3. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 443 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 444 5. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 445 6. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 446 7. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 447 8. **Does the preview environment match Figma at the defined breakpoints?** 448 9. **For a ui-kit component: right folder, right casing, right styling surface?** 449 `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx`, styled by a recipe. A 450 `.styles.ts`, a `cssVars`-style helper, a new `.zimm-*` class, or inline styles all mean the same 451 conversation — see "The atoms governance model" in Play 1. 452 453 --- 454 455 ## Play 5b — Verifying a design claim before you act on it 456 457 *Learned the expensive way on the footer build. Four times a conclusion reversed once the source was 458 actually read, and each reversal would have shipped a wrong change.* 459 460 ### Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision 461 462 `f2r/02-design/specs/` files carry `` and a `Status: draft` 463 header. They are **mechanical dumps of a Figma node**, not rulings. When the text-input spec had no 464 `clearable` attribute, that meant the Figma component doesn't have one — not that the design system had 465 ruled one out. Treating it as a ruling nearly deleted a control rather than making it opt-in. 466 467 Same trap in the other direction: the spec *did* define `trailing-icon`, which settled a question two 468 code comments had recorded backwards. 469 470 ### A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source 471 472 `header.ts` carried `width: min(597px, 60vw)` with a comment deriving 597 from 70 and the aspect ratio. 473 Grepping `overrides/` and `.docs/` for `597` returned three hits: the definition, its own comment, and one 474 copy. **No Figma node, no ticket, nothing.** A "fix" to make the header logo honour that value would have 475 been shipping a number nobody had ever approved. 476 477 Contrast the icon geometry: `327px`/`39px` cite Figma nodes in their comment, and the nodes check out. 478 479 **The test:** can you name the node or the doc? If not, it's a guess someone typed, however confident the 480 surrounding comment sounds. 481 482 ### Ask for the node. It costs the designer thirty seconds. 483 484 Four times on this build the answer came from reading a Figma node directly — the chevron geometry, the 485 four chevron rotations, the site-map item heights, the subscribe heading binding. Each took one message. 486 Each replaced a derivation I would otherwise have defended with arithmetic. 487 488 Deriving is legitimate when the source *shows* the derivation — all four chevrons export an identical 489 path, so Figma itself is rotating one glyph, and reproducing that is reading, not guessing. Deriving from 490 "it's probably the same as the other one" is not. 491 492 ### An audit that matches on value alone will produce confident nonsense 493 494 A style-mirror check flagged three constants as duplicating existing tokens. All three were false: 495 496 | Flagged | Why it was wrong | 497 |---|---| 498 | `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-1200` | The token is **48px**. Swapping would have broken WCAG 1.4.4 — px doesn't scale with zoom | 499 | `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-3500` | Same — the token is 140px | 500 | `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm` | Coincidence. A modal width has no relationship to a breakpoint | 501 502 The checker normalised units and ignored semantic role. Two of the three "fixes" would have been 503 regressions. **Before acting on a tooling finding, confirm the thing it matched is the thing it means.** 504 505 ### A grep count is not a coverage verdict 506 507 A prop-vs-story audit reported `trailing` as having "zero story coverage", and I reported it as a gap. It 508 was covered — by three `play` functions in the molecule that fills the slot, which is the correct level 509 for a slot prop. The same audit missed a story that *does* test a clear button, because the story matches 510 on `/clear input/i` and the grep was case-sensitive on the aria-label. 511 512 Both errors have one shape: **a proxy reported as the finding.** When a check returns zero, establish 513 which zero it is — untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. 514 515 ### A passing test can be encoding the bug 516 517 Phase 3 asserted `contact icons are not focusable` — green for weeks. The icons weren't focusable because 518 the hrefs were never wired through; the assertion had frozen a defect as expected behaviour. Wiring them 519 correctly turned the suite red. 520 521 Worth a standing question in review: *would this test still pass if the feature were broken in the 522 obvious way?* 523 524 --- 525 526 ## Play 6 — Accessibility 527 528 *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* 529 530 M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. 531 532 ### The per-component AC set (#12) 533 534 Standing list to apply to every component story: 535 536 - Keyboard operability and reachability 537 - Focus order and visible focus states 538 - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) 539 - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls 540 - Behaviour when optional content is absent 541 542 **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. 543 544 ### The one open item 545 546 M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. 547 548 **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. 549 550 --- 551 552 ## Play 7 — Page-level validation 553 554 *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* 555 556 M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. 557 558 ### Where each part lands today 559 560 | Ask | Home | 561 |---|---| 562 | Assembled UX / integration | ⚠️ Playwright E2E — the `@area` **vocabulary** is `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`, but only `@homepage` and `@checkout` are applied to any spec today. Five of the seven areas have no coverage at all | 563 | Performance | ✅ `lighthouserc.js` | 564 | Responsive behaviour | ⚠️ Partial — Playwright runs desktop + mobile Chrome, but asserts behaviour, not appearance | 565 | **Spacing / design fidelity / design parity** | ❌ **No automated home.** `testing.md` explicitly excludes visual snapshots from the Vitest budget | 566 567 **Name this rather than absorbing it.** Design-parity validation is currently manual visual QA. Either it's accepted as manual and the time is resourced, or it's a visual-regression tooling decision (Chromatic / Loki / Percy) — a new dependency and budget, which needs approval before anything is installed. An unresourced ask that quietly becomes yours is the failure mode here. 568 569 Operational note: only `e2e_homepage` is currently mapped in the change-scoping config. Each new area's first spec needs its own allow-list group, or it silently falls back to the full suite. 570 571 ### Incremental assembly (#15) 572 573 Tim's build → drop-in → verify loop is well supported and costs nothing to adopt: 574 575 | Step | Support | 576 |---|---| 577 | Build in isolation | Storybook — mandatory story; `Contentful/` category explicitly allows mock CMS data | 578 | Make available to authors | `npm run generate:contentful` regenerates definitions; pre-commit keeps it in sync | 579 | Author drops it on a page | Studio Experiences — appears once annotated | 580 | Verify | `pages/experience/` and `pages/contentfulPreview/` routes exist | 581 582 **Caveat worth stating:** this loop only works for Studio Experiences components. Entry-driven ones are wired in code and aren't drag-and-droppable. Another reason the pattern question in Play 8 matters. 583 584 --- 585 586 ## Play 8 — Pushing back before sizing 587 588 *Covers responsibility 14* 589 590 These were explicitly left unresolved. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. 591 592 | Open item | Position to hold | 593 |---|---| 594 | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | 595 | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | 596 | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | 597 | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | 598 | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | 599 | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | 600 | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | 601 | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | 602 603 ### The Figma link on the card is an input — treat it as one 604 605 The devs work from the Figma links on the Jira card via the Figma MCP. That makes the link a **build 606 input**, not a reference: whatever it points at is what gets coded, near-literally. 607 608 So a wrong or stale link doesn't produce a question — it produces a component built to the wrong design, 609 which then propagates: 610 611 - the **dev** builds the wrong thing, 612 - the **BA** signs off AC written against a different frame, 613 - **QA** tests against a third source, 614 615 and nobody discovers it until page assembly, by which point it's a defect against a 10-defect budget. 616 617 **Action:** where a card's Figma links are wrong, stale, or point at the wrong frame, go back to **Jas** and 618 ask for the card to be reworked with correct links rather than clarifying it verbally to one developer. 619 A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — the thing BA and QA both read — 620 still wrong. 621 622 Worth adding to the refinement checklist: **does the card carry a Figma link, and does it point at the 623 frame this story is actually about?** It's a ten-second check that removes a whole class of misalignment. 624 625 **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. 626 627 --- 628 629 ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation 630 631 *Covers responsibility 7* 632 633 Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 634 635 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. **The registry reports 10 consumers** (`.claude/registry/components.md`, verified against `develop` 636 @ `2dfeb4d`), so adding the axis later touches ten call sites, not a handful. Re-check the number before 637 quoting it — the registry is regenerated on every `overrides/app/**` change. 638 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** 639 640 ### Missing tokens and misaligned designs — the standing route 641 642 **Anything the design system doesn't answer goes to Kiera. Nothing gets invented locally.** 643 644 Two categories, same destination: 645 646 | What you hit | Why it can't be solved in code | 647 |---|---| 648 | **A Figma value with no token** | `theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned. Adding a token locally forks the design system silently | 649 | **A design that contradicts the implemented tokens** | Someone has to decide which is right. A developer picking one is an undocumented decision that later reads as a bug | 650 651 Live examples to carry into the next design review, all currently flagged in-code rather than resolved: 652 653 - **Primary button hover is 2.96:1** — white on `#969696`, failing WCAG AA (needs 4.5:1). Known, logged, 654 still open. 655 - **No inverse focus-ring token**, so focus on a dark surface is invisible. 656 - **Button heights** — `50/41px` in `button.ts` vs `52/40px` from Handover, and `BTN_PADDING_Y` (`5px`) 657 has no Handover token at all. 658 - **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 text styles hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'` instead 659 of referencing the scale; Figma reportedly specifies 100%. Until it's decided, nav line-height renders 660 off-spec. 661 - **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named scale entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl` (32), 662 or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). 663 664 The pattern to reinforce with the team: **flag it in-code with a comment naming the open question, and 665 raise it — don't silently pick a number.** That's already the convention; it's working, and it's worth 666 praising when you see it, because the alternative is invisible. 667 668 More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. 669 670 --- 671 672 ## Who owns what — and the session to settle it 673 674 The plays above assume a clear escalation route for each kind of problem. In practice the ownership 675 boundaries between FED, design and BA are not agreed, which is why the same question reaches different 676 people and gets different answers. 677 678 **Action: run an alignment session with Tash, Kiera and Hannah to establish who owns what.** Not a status 679 meeting — a boundary-setting one. The output is a single line per category naming the owner. 680 681 Working view going in, to be confirmed or corrected in the session: 682 683 | Category | Working owner | Route | 684 |---|---|---| 685 | Design system, tokens, missing values | **Kiera** | Standing design review — Play 9 | 686 | Design intent, misaligned or missing frames | **Kiera** | Same slot | 687 | Story content, AC, Figma links on the card | **Jas** | Rework the card, don't patch it verbally — Play 8 | 688 | Registry tooling, `shared/` coverage, override-first in F2R | **Han** | In flight — Play 1 | 689 | Component reuse, override-vs-build calls, PR quality | **You** | Plays 1 and 5 | 690 | Design-parity validation (who actually does the visual pass) | **Unassigned** | The sharp edge — Play 7 | 691 692 That last row is the one to force a decision on. Play 7 already notes design-parity validation has no 693 automated home and no named owner; combined with a 10-defect budget, "it quietly becomes the FED lead's 694 job" is the default outcome unless the session says otherwise. 695 696 Two dependencies worth tracking out of the same conversation: 697 698 - **Han's registry work** extends the generator to cover the `shared/` folder and bakes override-first 699 into the F2R workflow. Both reduce Play 1's manual load — worth knowing when they land so the playbook 700 can stop asking you to do it by hand. 701 - **The Figma-link quality issue** (Play 8) needs Jas to own card correctness, not just card creation. 702 703 --- 704 705 ## Guardrails 706 707 Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. 708 709 **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. 710 711 **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. 712 713 **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. 714 715 **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. 716 717 **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. 718 719 **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. 720 721 --- 722 723 ## Standing artifacts you own 724 725 | Artifact | Cadence | 726 |---|---| 727 | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | 728 | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | 729 | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | 730 | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | 731 | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | 732 | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | 733 734 --- 735 736 ## First two weeks 737 738 Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. 739 740 **Week 1** 741 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 742 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 743 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 744 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item 745 746 **Week 2** 747 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 748 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 749 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review — plus the token gaps in Play 9 750 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 751 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision 752 753 **Also, and not optional given the defect budget** 754 755 10. **Run the ownership alignment session** with Tash, Kiera and Hannah — and force a decision on who owns 756 design-parity validation. Everything else in this playbook has a named owner; that one doesn't. 757 11. **Ask Jas to rework any card whose Figma links are wrong or stale.** It's the cheapest defect 758 prevention available — the links are a build input, not a reference. 759 12. **Set the "green locally before opening a PR" expectation once, to the whole team.** `tsc`, lint, 760 tests. Said once as a standard, it costs nothing; enforced per-PR, it costs an hour each time. 761 13. **Say the override-first default out loud in refinement**, with the reason — overrides inherit the 762 hooks and wiring, bespoke builds re-derive them invisibly. 763 764 **Decisions now landed — three follow-ups to close them out** 765 766 14. **Amend `overrideStyling.md`'s justification for removing the `.zimm-btn-*` classes.** As written it 767 says a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`"* — which is simply 768 untrue of plain CSS, and anyone who notices can dismiss the whole rule. The real reasons are that two 769 surfaces for one component drift, and a class can't see the Chakra token layer. Also fold in the 770 atoms/molecules folder + casing decision. **Tier 1 governance file** — your verified-session exception 771 applies, but name the file and the reason. 772 15. **Coordinate the F2R conversion with Han before his 16 components land.** They're at 773 `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/zimm-button/` (kebab) with co-located 774 `.styles.ts`. Two mechanical changes: rename to camelCase, and convert each `.styles.ts` into a 775 recipe — class blocks become `baseStyle`/`variants`/`sizes`, `:hover` becomes `_hover`, native element 776 becomes the `chakra()` factory. **Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files** — they're a faithful 777 Figma→CSS transcription and the best raw material anyone has for writing the recipes. 778 His branch also predates #56 and carries its own `theme/foundation/`, so expect a real conflict there 779 too. Raise both before more work stacks on it. 780 16. **Settle `ui-kits` vs `uiKits`.** By the letter of `conventions.md` the grouping folder should be 781 camelCase like everything else Zimmermann-authored; both #55 and Han use `ui-kits`. Either rename it 782 while renaming Han's anyway, or record it as a documented exception — but don't leave it as an 783 accident, or the next person copies it and adds `ui-kits/form-fields/`. 784 785 --- 786 787 *Working document. The plays are grounded in what the two sessions actually asked for; the mechanics come from how this repo works today, so both will need updating as the tooling and the backlog move.* 788 789 *Verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d` on 18 August 2026. Confirmed accurate: every asserted repo path, 790 the base-capability claims (`product-view`'s `addToCart`/`updateCart`, `swatch-group`'s index/swatch/test, 791 `quantity-picker`, all three variant hooks), the ast-grep and semgrep rule ids, the absent ESLint 792 complexity rules, the bundlesize budgets, the four absolute files, and `shoppableImage` / 793 `pages/experience` / `pages/contentfulPreview`. Two figures were corrected in this pass — Button's 794 consumer count and the E2E area coverage. See the companion findings doc for the full V&V trail.* 795 796 *Updated 18 August 2026 with the UI-build additions: the 10-defect quality bar (§1), override-first as the 797 default (Play 1), gate-zero plus three-surface review and the token checklist (Play 5), Figma-link 798 correctness as a build input (Play 8), the design-system escalation route and live token gaps (Play 9), and 799 the ownership alignment session (new section). The token specifics reflect `develop` after PR #56 — check 800 `overrideStyling.md` before quoting them.* 801

file.content: # FED Lead Playbook **Derived from:** the two "Contentful v PWA Kit Components and User Story Alignment" sessions **Owner:** Marcel Navarro · **Started:** August 2026 **Companions:** [fedBuild-manual.md](./fedBuild-manual.md) (the developer-facing half — how to build) · [componentStories-BA-guide.md](./componentStories-BA-guide.md) (the BA-facing version) · [pr52-pr55-findings.md](./pr52-pr55-findings.md) (worked example of Play 5 applied to two live PRs) · `.docs/temp/{componentStoryReview,meeting2Prep,meeting2Analysis}.md` (the underlying analysis) **Authority on styling:** `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` in-repo — if this playbook and that file disagree, it wins. Purpose: the two sessions put sixteen things on your desk without saying when or how any of them get done. This turns that into a rhythm, a set of repeatable plays, and the specific mechanics for each. --- ## 1. It won't scale and it will slip. Play 1 handles this by moving the lookup to where the story is drafted and keeping only the judgement calls for yourself. ### The quality bar this all serves Everything below is calibrated to one number. **The SOW allows no more than 10 defects, and no Sev3.** Zimmermann is a luxury brand and is exceptionally particular about UI. That combination means the usual trade — ship it, fix it in QA — is not available here. A visual defect that would be a shrug on another project consumes part of a very small budget. Three consequences to plan around rather than discover: - **Vigilance is the job, not an overhead on the job.** Be as vigilant as possible, on every PR. - **Budget real time for checking.** A proper pass over a UI PR — preview environment, Figma, tokens, states, responsive — is **an hour or more**. Treat that as the cost of the review, not as slippage. - **Do as much as we can and flag the rest.** Where design is missing, ambiguous or contradictory, the answer is to raise it, not to invent a value. An invented value becomes a defect *and* a design-system divergence. --- ## 2. Your operating rhythm Sixteen responsibilities, four moments. Regenerated automatically by the pre-commit hook on any `overrides/app/**` change | | Same for hooks / utils / pages / routes | `.claude/registry/{hooks,utils,pages,routes}.md` | | What's in the base package? | `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/` and `/app/hooks/` | | Is it already claimed by a squad? | Registry `Squad` column · `.claude/rules/squadA.md` | | What tier am I about to touch? | Registry `Tier` column, or `/audit-tier` | The `Origin` column is doing most of the work: **`Base` means it exists but isn't scaffolded into `overrides/` yet** — which is a cost, not a free win (see below). ### Worked examples, already verified | Ask | What already exists | |---|---| | Size selector | Base `swatch-group/` — index, swatch, plus an existing test | | Add to bag | Base `product-view/index.jsx` — already does `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the button and label, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling, and an `updateCart` variant | | Max purchase quantity | Base `quantity-picker/` | | Variant resolution | `use-controlled-variations`, `use-derived-product`, `use-add-to-cart-modal` | Worth knowing before SFCC-650 is sized: its description says *"Cart API integration is in scope"*, but the base already performs the cart call. That story should read as **extend `product-view`**, not build cart integration. ### Override-first — why the second rung is where the value is The ladder says "reuse before build". The stronger version, and the one to hold the line on: **default to overriding the base component, not writing a new one.** The reason is not tidiness — it's that an override **inherits the wiring for free**. Override `product-view` and you get `addToCart([{product, variant, quantity}])`, the add-to-cart modal, bundle handling and `updateCart` already connected. Build a bespoke equivalent and every one of those has to be re-derived, re-tested and re-reviewed, and none of it is visible in the story points. There's a second-order effect worth naming in refinement. PWA Kit's resolver rewires imports transparently, so **overriding a component SFCC's own base components already import means the whole base template inherits your version** — no call sites touched. A bespoke component in a new folder reaches only the pages someone remembers to wire it into. Same visual result on the page you're building; very different coverage across the site. ⚠️ **One documented exception: `shared/ui/`.** That directory is consumed through a barrel (`shared/ui/index.jsx`), and the barrel's own re-exports are **relative** (`export {Button} from './Button'`). The `ccExtensibility` resolver only rewrites `@salesforce/retail-react-app/...` specifiers, so a relative import inside `node_modules` is never redirected. **208 base files import that barrel; none import `shared/ui/Button` directly — so overriding `shared/ui//` intercepts nothing.** It is a place to put raw Zimmermann primitives for *our own* code to import explicitly, not an interception point. See "Two component families" below. So the question in review isn't only "did you reuse?" but **"is this an override, and if not, why not?"** **In flight, and relevant:** Han is extending the registry generator to account for the `shared/` folder as well, and is building the override-first approach into the F2R workflow — so the default lands in the tooling rather than depending on everyone remembering it. Worth tracking; it removes work from Play 1. ### The hidden cost to name every time If `Origin = Base`, the component isn't in `overrides/` yet, and AGENTS.md's **Copy-first rule** applies before any functional work: 1. Copy base file → mirrored path in `overrides/` 2. Convert to TypeScript, fix imports 3. `npx tsc --noEmit` 4. Add a temporary `console.log` marker 5. **Stop — a human confirms the override renders instead of the base** 6. Then build; remove markers It's serialised and human-gated. **The first story against a given base component pays it; later ones don't.** This is the single most common reason a story looks small and isn't — exactly Jasmijn's concern. Either split it into an enabler story or size the first story accordingly. ### Making this scale (the fix for #1) Add one line to the BA prompt template in Confluence 274137093: > *"Check `.claude/registry/components.md` — does a Base, Override or Custom component already cover this? Report Origin, Tier, Squad and Consumer count."* That makes four of the six refinement questions self-service. You keep the two that need judgement: - **Is extending the base the right call, or is a Zimmermann-specific build justified?** - **Is the design-system prerequisite real, or can we proceed?** ### Preventing duplicate atoms (#3, #8) The atoms question — *"when does an atom deserve its own story?"* — is largely already answered by existing convention rather than needing a new model: - A story is required for anything **exported from its folder** under `overrides/app/components/` or `/pages/`. - **Not** required for internal sub-components that only render inside one parent — cover their variants via the parent's stories. - The Storybook categorisation (`Foundation / Elements / Layout / Commerce / Forms / Pages / Contentful`) gives you the vocabulary: `Elements/` *is* the atoms layer. Applied to 04.7's `↳ Sub-component` rows: Pause/Play, Footer Item, Footer Textfield, Icons don't each need a story unless independently reusable. Without that rule the Footer alone generates four. ### The atoms governance model — decided (closes #8) Three developers independently inferred three different answers from the same rules file, so this is now written down. Both halves are settled; the developer-facing version is in the FED Build Manual §3. **Where they live, and what they're called** ``` overrides/app/components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx ``` **camelCase, one folder per component.** These are Zimmermann-authored, so `conventions.md`'s default applies; the kebab-case rule is scoped to files *mirroring a base Salesforce file*, and no `@salesforce/…/zimm-button` exists to mirror. It also satisfies `components.md`'s named-export-matches-folder rule. Precedents: `pageContainer/`, `pdpProductInfo/`. Three casings coexist and each is right in its own family — worth stating in review, because generalising from one to another is the mistake people make: | Family | Casing | Why | |---|---|---| | SFCC override | `product-tile/` kebab | Upstream imports that exact path | | ui-kit component | **`zimmButton/` camelCase** | Zimmermann-authored — the default | | `shared/ui` primitive | `Button/` PascalCase | Mirrors upstream's own casing | **Tiering** is by what the component's own template renders — atom renders nothing, molecule renders only atoms, organism renders at least one molecule. An icon passed as a prop doesn't count; slotted children don't count. Tier follows composition, not pixel size. The F2R contract already records this as `composes: [...]` and machine-checks it in `02-design/library/contract/validate.mjs`, so **use the contract's tier rather than re-deriving it in refinement.** **The styling surface: a theme recipe, always.** | Case | Surface | |---|---| | It **is** a Chakra component | `theme/components/.ts` recipe; `variant`/`size` resolve automatically | | **Bespoke multipart** Zimmermann component | Recipe + register + `useMultiStyleConfig` + `chakra()` factory | | Static, non-interactive, heavily reused | `.zimm-*` class in `globalStyles.ts` | | Nothing else fits | `sx`, then co-located `.scss` — last resort | `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` is the worked example for the bespoke case. The `chakra()` factory is what makes it possible to style a native element from a recipe — that was the missing piece people kept hitting. **The argument to use when someone proposes co-located CSS instead** (and it will come up, because plain CSS handles `:hover` perfectly well): a stylesheet can only see `var(--zimm-*)`, which is *derived output*. Authoring there forfeits `textStyle`, the named `theme.space` scale, semantic colour tokens, responsive arrays and the 125 drift-guard tests. It's not bad CSS — it's the wrong end of the token pipeline. --- ## Play 2 — Estimation validation *Covers responsibilities 5, 16* Run this before sprint planning, not in it. ### The re-baseline to communicate once M2 concluded pages become assemblies. The honest consequence: - **Homepage / page estimates should go down.** Composition genuinely is cheaper. - **Component estimates should go up by more than the pages save.** Because a component story now carries: all variants upfront + accessibility AC + a mandatory Storybook story + a test where logic-heavy + Copy-first scaffolding on first touch. If only the first half of that lands, the programme will look like it got faster and won't have. Say this out loud in planning — once, clearly. ### Split the two kinds of effort (#16) | Component build | Page composition | |---|---| | Real frontend development | Assembly and configuration | | Variants, states, accessibility | Integration testing | | Storybook + tests | Visual validation | | Sized as build work | Sized as validation work | Don't let them be estimated with the same scale. ### Challenge list For each story before it's sized: - [ ] `Origin = Base`? → Copy-first cost is in, or split out - [ ] All variants captured, or only the ones on the first page? - [ ] Accessibility written as AC, or assumed? - [ ] Storybook story accounted for? - [ ] Designs confirmed, or still in progress? (04.7 status column) - [ ] Does it depend on anything in Play 8's open list? - [ ] Composition variant hiding as a configuration variant? (Play 3) --- ## Play 3 — Component completeness & variant review *Covers responsibilities 9, 11* M2's rule: a component isn't complete until it covers all supported variants, and the page just configures it. One Editorial Card, not a Homepage one and a PLP one. ### The distinction to hold | Kind | Examples | How it's built | |---|---|---| | **Configuration variant** | text alignment, CTA on/off, title on/off, body copy present/absent | Props on one component ✅ Tim's rule applies directly | | **Composition variant** | 1 vs 2 column, 3-up vs 4-up grids | A **container/slot component** — structurally a second component | This matters because a composition variant priced as a prop will be under-estimated. On the Studio Experiences path especially, a repeating structure can't be a prop — the composition primitive is `children`. So "one Editorial Card with all variants" often resolves to *two* components: the card, plus a container holding one or two. Better outcome — the container is reusable anywhere — but it changes the count. Catch it at refinement. ### Why "upfront" is a hard requirement here, not a preference The Contentful sync is **additive-only — it cannot delete a field from a published content type**. Getting the variant model wrong isn't rework, it's semi-permanent. This is the strongest argument you have for holding the line on variant completeness, and it supports Tim's position rather than fighting it. ### Optional-field handling (#11) M2: don't assume CMS fields are populated. Every Contentful-backed component needs AC for the absent case — no empty space, no placeholder, no layout break. Make it a standing question in refinement rather than a per-story discovery. --- ## Play 4 — The renderer contract *Covers responsibility 10* M2 asked for "a standard renderer contract between Contentful models and React components." This is the artifact that makes the Contentful story and the PWA Kit story independently workable — without it they drift, and additive-only sync makes drift expensive. **The requirement it satisfies:** `02-contentful.md` §2 — *"TypeScript types match the Contentful field IDs exactly, so schema drift is caught at compile time."* **The artifact:** one table, identical in both stories of every Contentful pair. | Field ID | Display name | Type / control | Required | Localised | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | `image` | Image | Media | Yes | No | | | `imageAlt` | Image Alt Text | shortText | No | Yes | behaviour when empty — see Play 6 | | `bodyCopy` | Body Copy | longText | No | Yes | | | `ctaLabel` | CTA Label | shortText | No | Yes | CTA renders only if label **and** URL set | | `ctaUrl` | CTA URL | shortText | No | No | internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"` | **Field IDs, not display names.** "Body copy" in prose is where drift starts. **You own the template; the BA fills it; you sign off the field IDs before the Contentful story is built.** That signature is the cheapest possible insurance against an undeletable wrong field. **Note for the ordering question:** for Studio Experiences components the contract is generated from the React props rather than authored first — so the review point moves to the component's prop type. Which pattern a given component uses is still unresolved (Play 8). --- ## Play 5 — PR review *Covers responsibility 4* The useful move here is knowing what the tooling already catches, so your attention goes where it's actually needed. ### Already mechanical — don't spend review time on it | Check | Enforced by | |---|---| | Missing `alt` on `` | ast-grep `img-missing-alt` | | `IconButton` without `aria-label` | ast-grep `icon-button-missing-aria-label` | | `onClick` on non-interactive element without `role` | ast-grep `clickable-non-interactive-element` | | Payment credentials logged | semgrep `payment-credential-logged` | | Unsanitised `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` | semgrep `dangerously-set-inner-html-unsanitized` | | Type errors, lint, conventional commits | `tsc --noEmit`, lint, commit-msg hook | | Registry freshness | pre-commit hook | ### Not enforced — this is your list | Gap | Why it matters | |---|---| | **Hardcoded hex / px values** in Chakra props and `.scss` | `css.md` states plainly it isn't mechanically enforced. Highest-frequency design-system violation | | **Component complexity / size** | No `complexity` or `max-lines-per-function` in `.eslintrc.js` — confirmed | | **Chakra `` without alt** | The ast-grep rule matches lowercase `` only. Every Contentful component here uses `` — so the guard doesn't cover the component family under discussion | | **Duplication / reuse** | No tool detects "this is a second Button". This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human | | **Salesforce alignment** | Whether base capability was leveraged — judgement only | Two of these are cheap to close, and the repo's own rules files already recommend the fix: an ast-grep rule for hardcoded design values, and the two ESLint core rules. **Both touch Tier 1 files** — raise as a decision, don't land quietly. See §Guardrails. ### Gate zero — does it actually build? **Check this before spending review attention on anything else.** A PR has already been opened on this project with a failing typecheck — missing type declarations that the branch itself had previously supplied and lost in a merge. Reviewing the design of code that doesn't compile wastes the expensive part of your day. ```bash npx tsc --noEmit # must be clean npm run lint # separate real errors from auto-fixable prettier noise npx vitest run ``` Two things worth knowing about this failure mode, because it will recur: - **A merge can silently delete a declaration.** When a branch merges `develop` and both sides touched the same ambient-types file, the merge can resolve to develop's version and drop what the branch added. It typechecks on neither side's intent and nobody notices until CI or a local build. - **It isn't always the author's mistake.** In that instance a second error came from following a repo rules file that named a package which doesn't exist on the installed Storybook major. Check whether the rule or the code is wrong before raising it as a code finding. Make "green locally before opening" the expectation, and say so once to the whole team rather than per-PR. It isn't about blame — it's that the review budget is an hour per PR and this spends it on nothing. ### Review across three surfaces, not one Reading the diff is the smallest part. For any UI PR, look at all three: | Surface | What only it will tell you | |---|---| | **The diff** | Tokens vs literals, reuse vs reimplementation, abstractions respected | | **The preview environment** | What it actually renders — states, responsive behaviour, whether hover/focus work at all | | **Figma** | Whether the rendered output matches the design, and which gaps are design gaps rather than build gaps | Every `feature/*` and `fix/*` branch now auto-deploys to its own MRT environment and posts the URL on the PR. There is no longer a reason to review a UI change from the diff alone — **open the environment and put it beside Figma.** If no URL comment appeared, the branch had no open PR when it was pushed; a further push once the PR exists will post it. Evaluate the rendered output against Figma deliberately, at the breakpoints the design defines. Anything that doesn't line up is either a build finding or a design gap — and separating those two is your call, not the developer's. ### Tokens and CSS — the highest-yield thing you check This is where divergence starts, it is not mechanically enforced, and both PRs currently in flight have drifted in different directions. Be deliberately vigilant here. `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md` is the authority. The hierarchy, in order: 1. `textStyle` for anything textual — **never** a raw `fontSize` 2. Semantic token strings — `color="text.default"`, `padding="m"` 3. The component's own `theme/components/.ts` for variant / size / state 4. `sx` only for a genuine prop-system gap 5. Scoped `.scss` only when `sx` truly can't express it What to actively look for: - **The correct token, not just a token.** A value that resolves to the right pixels via the wrong token passes a casual glance and breaks the moment the design system moves. Two `sx` blocks recently hand-rebuilt what `textStyle="heading3"` and `textStyle="body2"` already provide, property for property. - **`var(--zimm-*)` in the right layer.** It is the convention *inside* `theme/components/*.ts`. In component JSX it is not — that's rungs 1 and 2. Seeing `var()` in a `.tsx` is a signal to look closer. - **`--zimm-scale-NNN` numeric aliases in JSX.** They exist only for the `.zimm-*` global classes. The named scale (`m`, `l`, `xl`) is the Chakra-facing surface. - **A theme recipe that nothing consumes.** A `theme/components/.ts` file that is written and registered but never read via `useStyleConfig` looks like compliance and is dead code. - **A second copy of the token registry.** Any new utility that re-types token names as strings reintroduces exactly the drift the derived-token work removed. - **Interaction states in JavaScript.** `useState` for hover / press / focus instead of `_hover` / `_active` / `_focusVisible` means those states are dead until hydration, sticky on touch, and unreachable by the theme. ### Tests and stories — the minimum, while UI is the focus The build focus is UI, and that's fine — but don't let coverage reach zero on the way through: - **Unit tests where they earn their place** — data mapping, transforms, non-obvious logic. Not for re-exports or passthroughs. - **At minimum, scaffold the Storybook story.** Every component exported from its folder needs one. A scaffolded story with a `Default` export and the meaningful states is the floor, even if the `play` function comes later. It's also the surface your own review depends on. ### Review questions, in order 0. **Does it build?** `tsc`, lint, tests — gate zero above 1. Was an existing component / hook / utility reused, or is this a second implementation? 2. **Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?** 3. Are all design values tokens — and the *correct* tokens, in the correct layer? 4. Does it respect existing abstractions, or work around them? 5. Was base Salesforce capability leveraged where it exists? 6. Accessibility: keyboard, focus order, states — beyond what ast-grep catches 7. Storybook story present? Test where logic-heavy? 8. **Does the preview environment match Figma at the defined breakpoints?** 9. **For a ui-kit component: right folder, right casing, right styling surface?** `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}//index.tsx`, styled by a recipe. A `.styles.ts`, a `cssVars`-style helper, a new `.zimm-*` class, or inline styles all mean the same conversation — see "The atoms governance model" in Play 1. --- ## Play 5b — Verifying a design claim before you act on it *Learned the expensive way on the footer build. Four times a conclusion reversed once the source was actually read, and each reversal would have shipped a wrong change.* ### Absence in an extracted spec is not a decision `f2r/02-design/specs/` files carry `` and a `Status: draft` header. They are **mechanical dumps of a Figma node**, not rulings. When the text-input spec had no `clearable` attribute, that meant the Figma component doesn't have one — not that the design system had ruled one out. Treating it as a ruling nearly deleted a control rather than making it opt-in. Same trap in the other direction: the spec *did* define `trailing-icon`, which settled a question two code comments had recorded backwards. ### A value in the codebase is not a spec until you find its source `header.ts` carried `width: min(597px, 60vw)` with a comment deriving 597 from 70 and the aspect ratio. Grepping `overrides/` and `.docs/` for `597` returned three hits: the definition, its own comment, and one copy. **No Figma node, no ticket, nothing.** A "fix" to make the header logo honour that value would have been shipping a number nobody had ever approved. Contrast the icon geometry: `327px`/`39px` cite Figma nodes in their comment, and the nodes check out. **The test:** can you name the node or the doc? If not, it's a guess someone typed, however confident the surrounding comment sounds. ### Ask for the node. It costs the designer thirty seconds. Four times on this build the answer came from reading a Figma node directly — the chevron geometry, the four chevron rotations, the site-map item heights, the subscribe heading binding. Each took one message. Each replaced a derivation I would otherwise have defended with arithmetic. Deriving is legitimate when the source *shows* the derivation — all four chevrons export an identical path, so Figma itself is rotating one glyph, and reproducing that is reading, not guessing. Deriving from "it's probably the same as the other one" is not. ### An audit that matches on value alone will produce confident nonsense A style-mirror check flagged three constants as duplicating existing tokens. All three were false: | Flagged | Why it was wrong | |---|---| | `SPACE_SECTION = '3rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-1200` | The token is **48px**. Swapping would have broken WCAG 1.4.4 — px doesn't scale with zoom | | `SIZE_COL_NAV = '8.75rem'` ≡ `--zimm-scale-3500` | Same — the token is 140px | | `SIZE_MODAL_SUB = '30rem'` ≡ `breakpoints.sm` | Coincidence. A modal width has no relationship to a breakpoint | The checker normalised units and ignored semantic role. Two of the three "fixes" would have been regressions. **Before acting on a tooling finding, confirm the thing it matched is the thing it means.** ### A grep count is not a coverage verdict A prop-vs-story audit reported `trailing` as having "zero story coverage", and I reported it as a gap. It was covered — by three `play` functions in the molecule that fills the slot, which is the correct level for a slot prop. The same audit missed a story that *does* test a clear button, because the story matches on `/clear input/i` and the grep was case-sensitive on the aria-label. Both errors have one shape: **a proxy reported as the finding.** When a check returns zero, establish which zero it is — untested, tested elsewhere, or unused. ### A passing test can be encoding the bug Phase 3 asserted `contact icons are not focusable` — green for weeks. The icons weren't focusable because the hrefs were never wired through; the assertion had frozen a defect as expected behaviour. Wiring them correctly turned the suite red. Worth a standing question in review: *would this test still pass if the feature were broken in the obvious way?* --- ## Play 6 — Accessibility *Covers responsibilities 6, 12* M1 and M2 both landed on accessibility living **inside** component stories, as AC, not as a follow-up task. ### The per-component AC set (#12) Standing list to apply to every component story: - Keyboard operability and reachability - Focus order and visible focus states - Interaction states (hover, active, disabled, focused) - Screen-reader behaviour for images and icon-only controls - Behaviour when optional content is absent **Baseline is WCAG 2.2 AA**, falling back to 2.1 only where 2.2 is technically infeasible *and* the reason is documented. Worth correcting on SFCC-648, which currently commits to 2.1 AA — and setting 2.2 as the story-template default so it doesn't propagate. ### The one open item M2 landed on: *if alt text exists render it; if not, don't render the attribute.* There's a real technical problem with that — omitting the attribute makes assistive tech treat the image as meaningful-but-undescribed, and it commonly reads out the filename; `alt=""` removes it from the accessibility tree entirely. The existing draft AC on the render story already says the latter. **Your action:** get it confirmed with Tim before it propagates into every image-bearing component. Frame it as the content-model question it really is — *how do we distinguish "intentionally decorative" from "someone forgot"?* — which is a Contentful field decision (required alt, or an explicit decorative toggle), not a renderer decision. The BA guide flags it as pending rather than settled. --- ## Play 7 — Page-level validation *Covers responsibilities 13, 15* M2 kept page validation with FED even though pages stop being development units: spacing, layout, design fidelity, responsive behaviour, assembled UX. ### Where each part lands today | Ask | Home | |---|---| | Assembled UX / integration | ⚠️ Playwright E2E — the `@area` **vocabulary** is `homepage, checkout, search, account, pdp, plp, integrations`, but only `@homepage` and `@checkout` are applied to any spec today. Your job is to keep them from being sized on assumption. | Open item | Position to hold | |---|---| | **Alt text** | Confirm with Tim before it lands in AC — Play 6 | | **External links** | Already answered in draft AC (internal → same tab; external → new tab + `rel="noopener noreferrer"`). Adopt it, bake it into the Link component when built. Doesn't need another meeting | | **Recommendations** | Not actually unknown — `SFCC-7` already holds eight decomposed, requirement-traced tickets (112, 118, 119, 313, 314, 642, 647, plus 301 under Cart). **SFCC-647 is already `Ready for Development`** and is the one that answers the data-source question. All are Priority `Low`, which is why they surfaced as unknowns. Raise 647; don't create tickets | | **Shop the Look naming** | Four names in circulation for possibly two things: "Shop the Look" (M2 + SFCC-90), "Shop the Edit" (SFCC-313), "Product Cards with Lookbook" (04.7, marked Done), and `shoppableImage` (which already exists in code and delivers exactly the manual curation Bianca described). Resolve to one name per capability before estimating | | **Preview & publishing** | Documented: the preview token is set on dev/test/sit/uat only, never staging or prod; both preview paths 404 without it and are `noindex`. **Authors preview on `uat`.** Settle it now — "can we preview on prod?" is a likely later ask, and it needs a Tier 1 change against a documented security rationale | | **Contentful pattern per component** | Still unresolved after two sessions, and it decides story order, whether the incremental-assembly loop is available, and whether a component is buildable as specified. **Highest-value item to close** | | **`regions` content-model field** | Unconfirmed, and it affects every Contentful component's variant model across 8 storefronts. Prerequisite to "design variants upfront" | | **Composed-page ownership** | Tim's *"not product/category → Contentful"* rule is a good default but doesn't settle PDP/PLP editorial blocks, category landing pages, or promotional tiles in navigation. Category landing pages are the sharp edge, and PLP work is already in flight | ### The Figma link on the card is an input — treat it as one The devs work from the Figma links on the Jira card via the Figma MCP. That makes the link a **build input**, not a reference: whatever it points at is what gets coded, near-literally. So a wrong or stale link doesn't produce a question — it produces a component built to the wrong design, which then propagates: - the **dev** builds the wrong thing, - the **BA** signs off AC written against a different frame, - **QA** tests against a third source, and nobody discovers it until page assembly, by which point it's a defect against a 10-defect budget. **Action:** where a card's Figma links are wrong, stale, or point at the wrong frame, go back to **Jas** and ask for the card to be reworked with correct links rather than clarifying it verbally to one developer. A verbal fix repairs one person's understanding and leaves the card — the thing BA and QA both read — still wrong. Worth adding to the refinement checklist: **does the card carry a Figma link, and does it point at the frame this story is actually about?** It's a ten-second check that removes a whole class of misalignment. **A process note worth acting on.** The Size Selector / Add To Bag split was argued and settled in a Jira comment thread two weeks before M1 re-derived it. Decisions made in refinement need somewhere findable to live, or they get re-litigated. Cheapest fix: when a decision lands, it goes on the story *and* into the relevant Confluence page — not just the thread. --- ## Play 9 — Design-system escalation *Covers responsibility 7* Standing agenda for the design review with Kiera. Two concrete items rather than a general "validate button states": 1. **Button** — 04.7 lists *"Style: Primary, Secondary · Size: Large, Small · Colour: Normal, Inverse"* and marks it Done. The implemented component exposes `variant: 'primary'|'secondary'` and `size: 'lg'|'sm'` — **no Colour axis.** Worth noting the *states* are fine (hover, active, disabled, focus-visible are all defined for both variants), so "disabled variants" isn't the gap; the Colour axis is. **The registry reports 10 consumers** (`.claude/registry/components.md`, verified against `develop` @ `2dfeb4d`), so adding the axis later touches ten call sites, not a handful. Re-check the number before quoting it — the registry is regenerated on every `overrides/app/**` change. 2. **Icon Button** — same Inventory spec, also marked Done, **no implementation at all.** ### Missing tokens and misaligned designs — the standing route **Anything the design system doesn't answer goes to Kiera. Nothing gets invented locally.** Two categories, same destination: | What you hit | Why it can't be solved in code | |---|---| | **A Figma value with no token** | `theme/foundation/` is Tier 1 and designer-owned. Adding a token locally forks the design system silently | | **A design that contradicts the implemented tokens** | Someone has to decide which is right. A developer picking one is an undocumented decision that later reads as a bug | Live examples to carry into the next design review, all currently flagged in-code rather than resolved: - **Primary button hover is 2.96:1** — white on `#969696`, failing WCAG AA (needs 4.5:1). Known, logged, still open. - **No inverse focus-ring token**, so focus on a dark surface is invisible. - **Button heights** — `50/41px` in `button.ts` vs `52/40px` from Handover, and `BTN_PADDING_Y` (`5px`) has no Handover token at all. - **`textStyles.navigation`** is the only one of 22 text styles hardcoding `lineHeight: 'normal'` instead of referencing the scale; Figma reportedly specifies 100%. Until it's decided, nav line-height renders off-spec. - **Spacing gaps** — 28px and 44px are in use with no named scale entry between `xl` (24) and `2xl` (32), or `3xl` (40) and `4xl` (64). The pattern to reinforce with the team: **flag it in-code with a comment naming the open question, and raise it — don't silently pick a number.** That's already the convention; it's working, and it's worth praising when you see it, because the alternative is invisible. More broadly: 04.7's status column marks components Done on *design* confirmation, which doesn't imply the implemented API matches. Worth agreeing what "Done" means in that column, since story writers are reading it as readiness. --- ## Who owns what — and the session to settle it The plays above assume a clear escalation route for each kind of problem. In practice the ownership boundaries between FED, design and BA are not agreed, which is why the same question reaches different people and gets different answers. **Action: run an alignment session with Tash, Kiera and Hannah to establish who owns what.** Not a status meeting — a boundary-setting one. The output is a single line per category naming the owner. Working view going in, to be confirmed or corrected in the session: | Category | Working owner | Route | |---|---|---| | Design system, tokens, missing values | **Kiera** | Standing design review — Play 9 | | Design intent, misaligned or missing frames | **Kiera** | Same slot | | Story content, AC, Figma links on the card | **Jas** | Rework the card, don't patch it verbally — Play 8 | | Registry tooling, `shared/` coverage, override-first in F2R | **Han** | In flight — Play 1 | | Component reuse, override-vs-build calls, PR quality | **You** | Plays 1 and 5 | | Design-parity validation (who actually does the visual pass) | **Unassigned** | The sharp edge — Play 7 | That last row is the one to force a decision on. Play 7 already notes design-parity validation has no automated home and no named owner; combined with a 10-defect budget, "it quietly becomes the FED lead's job" is the default outcome unless the session says otherwise. Two dependencies worth tracking out of the same conversation: - **Han's registry work** extends the generator to cover the `shared/` folder and bakes override-first into the F2R workflow. Both reduce Play 1's manual load — worth knowing when they land so the playbook can stop asking you to do it by hand. - **The Figma-link quality issue** (Play 8) needs Jas to own card correctness, not just card creation. --- ## Guardrails Things to respect while moving fast on all of the above. **Tier 1 files.** You hold tier-1-approver / admin, so the verified-session exception applies — you can proceed after naming the file and the reason. Relevant to Play 5's two proposed rules (`.coderabbit/`, `.eslintrc.js`) and to `.github/workflows/`. **Four files are absolute** — the exception does *not* apply regardless of approver status: `overrides/app/ssr.js`, `config/default.js`, `config/sites.js`, `worker/main.js`. **Branches.** Never work on `develop` or `main`. `release/*` is supervised — plan-first, confirm every edit, and code fixes go through a `fix/release-*` sub-branch. **Squad boundaries.** `header/`, `footer/`, `drawer-menu/`, `list-menu/` are shared shell — coordinate with the other squad before touching. `order-summary/` is Tier 2 and Squad B-notified. **Commits and PRs** only on explicit request — not as a "natural next step" after finishing work. **Scope.** Fixing a bug in a component doesn't license touching the hook it calls. Propose upward refactors; don't do them silently. --- ## Standing artifacts you own | Artifact | Cadence | |---|---| | Refinement checklist (Play 2's challenge list) | Keep current as patterns emerge | | Renderer contract template (Play 4) | Once; sign off per Contentful component | | Per-component accessibility AC set (Play 6) | Once; applied per story | | PR review question list (Play 5) | Review quarterly against what tooling now catches | | Open-items register (Play 8) | Update as items close | | Design-system gap list (Play 9) | Standing design-review agenda | --- ## First two weeks Sequenced by leverage — the first three unblock everything else. **Week 1** 1. Close the alt-text question with Tim before it propagates into AC 2. Get the Contentful pattern decision made (entry-driven vs Studio Experiences per component) — it blocks story order and buildability 3. Add the registry line to the BA prompt template — makes Play 1 self-service instead of making you a gate 4. Adopt the external-link standard from existing draft AC and close the item **Week 2** 5. Publish the renderer-contract template and use it on the next Contentful pair 6. Communicate the estimation re-baseline once, clearly, in planning 7. Take the two Button / Icon Button items to design review — plus the token gaps in Play 9 8. Raise SFCC-647 so the recommendations question resolves itself 9. Put the two enforcement rules up as a decision **Also, and not optional given the defect budget** 10. **Run the ownership alignment session** with Tash, Kiera and Hannah — and force a decision on who owns design-parity validation. Everything else in this playbook has a named owner; that one doesn't. 11. **Ask Jas to rework any card whose Figma links are wrong or stale.** It's the cheapest defect prevention available — the links are a build input, not a reference. 12. **Set the "green locally before opening a PR" expectation once, to the whole team.** `tsc`, lint, tests. Said once as a standard, it costs nothing; enforced per-PR, it costs an hour each time. 13. **Say the override-first default out loud in refinement**, with the reason — overrides inherit the hooks and wiring, bespoke builds re-derive them invisibly. **Decisions now landed — three follow-ups to close them out** 14. **Amend `overrideStyling.md`'s justification for removing the `.zimm-btn-*` classes.** As written it says a static class *"can't express `_hover`/`_active`/`_disabled`/`_focusVisible`"* — which is simply untrue of plain CSS, and anyone who notices can dismiss the whole rule. The real reasons are that two surfaces for one component drift, and a class can't see the Chakra token layer. Also fold in the atoms/molecules folder + casing decision. **Tier 1 governance file** — your verified-session exception applies, but name the file and the reason. 15. **Coordinate the F2R conversion with Han before his 16 components land.** They're at `components/ui-kits/{atoms,molecules,organisms}/zimm-button/` (kebab) with co-located `.styles.ts`. Two mechanical changes: rename to camelCase, and convert each `.styles.ts` into a recipe — class blocks become `baseStyle`/`variants`/`sizes`, `:hover` becomes `_hover`, native element becomes the `chakra()` factory. **Don't discard the `.styles.ts` files** — they're a faithful Figma→CSS transcription and the best raw material anyone has for writing the recipes. His branch also predates #56 and carries its own `theme/foundation/`, so expect a real conflict there too. Raise both before more work stacks on it. 16. **Settle `ui-kits` vs `uiKits`.** By the letter of `conventions.md` the grouping folder should be camelCase like everything else Zimmermann-authored; both #55 and Han use `ui-kits`. Either rename it while renaming Han's anyway, or record it as a documented exception — but don't leave it as an accident, or the next person copies it and adds `ui-kits/form-fields/`. --- *Working document. content.content:
=== PR ===
{"baseRefName":"develop","body":"# Description

Builds the global footer per SFCC-55 — shell, layout, and component structure across
all eight storefronts and both breakpoints. Content is Contentful-shaped but
fixture-backed: the CMS integration, link destinations, and Omneo sign-up are
separate stories, so `FooterContainer` supplies `FOOTER_FIXTURE` and `Footer` itself
takes its content as a required prop and fetches nothing.

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

# Linked

- Ticket: **SFCC-55** (Global Footer UI). Design: Figma *Zimmermann_Design_System_2026*;
  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3

# Squad ownership

- [x] Squad B

# Types of Changes

- [x] **New feature** (non-breaking change that adds functionality)

# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke
- `theme/components/zimmTextInput.ts` — colour derivation moved out of the hook into the
  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface
- `scripts/generateRegistry.mjs` — prop extraction scoped to `<ComponentName>Props`,
  Markdown table cells escaped, comma-containing types no longer silently dropped

# How to test-drive this PR

- `npm run env -- dev && npm start` → `/`, scroll to the footer. Nav columns hug their
  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it
- Resize through **1030px → 760px** — the bottom bar stays aligned with the content above
  it at every width
- Type a valid email → `>` opens the Join Us modal; empty or malformed is blocked inline
  with no modal
- `npm run storybook` → `Layout/Footer` (4 states incl. modal-open), `Elements/ZimmNavItem`
  (unsafe-href fallback), `Forms/ZimmInputAction` (validation)

# Protection-tier check

> ⚠️ **Tier 1** — `.storybook/{main.js,preview.tsx}` (test config, **Integration-owned**)
> for serving and mounting the self-hosted fonts; `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md`
> (governance, **both squad leads + Integration lead**) to record them;
> `theme/foundation/sizes.ts` (design system, **UI-Designer-owned**) — whitespace only,
> and it now diffs to **zero** against `develop`.
> Authenticated as `marcelannavarro`, a member of `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers`.
>
> ⚠️ **Tier 2** — `components/footer/`, `components/header/` (comments only),
> `theme/components/` (**UI-Designer — notified**). `components/footer/` is Global Shell,
> owned by **both squads** — Squad A notified.

# Testing

- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- [x] `npm run lint` — 0 errors (3 pre-existing `header` unused-import warnings, documented in-file)
- [x] `npm run test` (Vitest) — 168/168
- [x] Storybook interaction — 15 `play` functions across 7 stories
- [x] Runtime behaviour — 20/20 (hover, focus-visible, validation, modal focus trap + Escape + focus restore, overlay z-index above the sticky header)
- [x] Figma geometry — structural paddings exact at 64/48, 48/48, 24/24
- [x] Box model — 112 footer elements × 6 viewports, 0 off-token paddings/margins/gaps/borders
- [x] Accessibility — axe 0 violations / 17 passes (wcag2a → 2.2aa)
- [x] Local CodeRabbit — no new findings

  - Added self-hosted Futura Round fonts for consistent application and Storybook typography.
- **Documentation**

- **Tests**

Six ui-kit atoms/molecules were built or completed alongside it — logo, icon,
nav-item, button, text-input, and the input-action molecule — all six consumed by
the footer.

Three points worth surfacing before review:

- **Fonts are now self-hosted**, reversing the position stated in #53. Futura Round
  renders in-app and in Storybook from one shared `@font-face` module. The fallback
  stack measures ~13% wider, so several sizing decisions made against it were wrong
  and were redone once real metrics were in play. Licence files are deliberately
  excluded from the repository.
- **This branch was taken over from Jersey.** Their three CodeRabbit-fix commits are
  in the history; the parts worth keeping were adopted deliberately as separate
  commits (`fix(button)`, `feat(footer)`, `test(ui-kit)`) rather than folded into
  conflict resolution, so what came from upstream and why stays visible.
- **9 of the 16 new commits carry `.claude/registry/` churn.** The `pre-commit` hook
  regenerates it on any `components/`/`hooks/`/`utils/` change and `git add`s it.
  Mechanical — skip those hunks.

`header/index.tsx` carries a pre-existing `fontSize="l"` (invalid token) and a
`useCurrentBasket` call from the original copy-first import. Both predate this PR —
our diff there is comments only — but they surface in the changed-files view.

  footer frames signed off with Dani & Vicky (2026-07-07). Test cases SFCC-T116 – SFCC-T122
- Sprint: SFCC — Sprint 3
