# Changes

- `components/footer/` — footer assembly, subscribe section + modal, contact icon row,
  bottom bar; Contentful-shaped fixture and schema placeholder
- `theme/components/footer.ts` — the `ZimmFooter` multipart recipe. Named `ZimmFooter`,
  not `Footer`: `extendTheme` deep-merges, so a recipe sharing a base SFCC recipe's name
  inherits it rather than replacing it
- `components/ui-kits/` — six atoms/molecules; `cssVars` indirection removed in favour of
  the `--zimm-*` custom properties directly, and `utils/cssVars.ts` deleted
- `theme/fontFace.tsx` + `static/fonts/` — self-hosted Futura Round, mounted in both the
  app and Storybook from one module so the two cannot drift
- `components/icons/` — the four Zimmermann chevrons, replacing base-template
  substitutions that rendered a filled glyph where the design is a 1px stroke

  recipe, so the recipe is the single styling surface

  content with even gaps; hovering a link underlines it

  with no modal

-management system" — so `.woff2`/`.otf` must not be committed here or served from the MRT CDN.

+Futura Round faces — Regular 400 and Medium 500 — declared by
+`overrides/app/theme/fontFace.tsx` and mounted in both `_app-config/index.tsx` and
+`.storybook/preview.tsx`. Only two faces exist because only two are used: all 22 textStyles
+resolve to fontWeight 400 or 500, and `fonts.body === fonts.heading`.

+`foundation/fonts.ts` already lists `'Futura Round'` first in both stacks, so the `@font-face`
+declaration is the only thing that makes it resolve — no component, recipe or token changes.
+The fallback stack renders roughly 13% wider, which is why serving the real faces matters for
+design-parity review against Figma.

content.content:
===== .docs/temp/openItems.md =====
     155 .docs/temp/openItems.md
# Integration Open Items — Consolidated

> This is an aggregate of `.docs/integration` open items.

Open items requiring client confirmation across the fifteen external integrations in scope for the Zimmermann PWA storefront. Each item is a decision, contract, credential, or sign-off that must land before the corresponding integration can be implemented end-to-end against a real account.

## Summary

We need their documentations or implementation guide for at least:
Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).

Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.

Plus:

- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?

| #   | Integration | Items                  |
| --- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| 1   | SFCC        | 2                      |
| 2   | Contentful  | 3                      |
| 3   | MuleSoft    | 4                      |
| 4   | Omneo       | 3 (all hard blockers)  |
| 5   | GiveX       | 3                      |
| 6   | Booxi       | 4 (scope/timeline TBC) |
| 7   | Adyen       | 2                      |
| 8   | Global-e    | 2                      |
| 9   | Google Maps | 1                      |
| 10  | reCAPTCHA   | 2                      |
| 11  | Narvar      | 2                      |
| 12  | Didomi      | 2                      |
| 13  | GTM         | 2                      |
| 14  | Inside Chat | 2                      |
| 15  | Optimizely  | 1                      |
| 16  | Crazy Egg   | 3                      |
| 17  | Measmerize  | 1                      |
| 18  | Vimeo       | 2                      |

Total: 41 items across 18 integrations.

---

## 1. SFCC

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.

## 2. Contentful

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.

## 3. MuleSoft

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. Minor residual points to confirm with Tryzens: `channel.type` values for online orders (sample data only shows in-store); whether the returns endpoint supports `offset`/`count` pagination; the `shop.id` inconsistency between list (`"storefront-catalog-eu"`) and detail (`"ZIMMERMANN_LONDON_STORE"`) responses; the full set of `psp` values for online payment methods (sample shows `"cash"` and `"store_credit"` only).
4. **CAI-023 — warehouse + boutique stock aggregation for browse-level availability.** Confirm whether MuleSoft can deliver a pre-aggregated available-to-promise figure combining warehouse and eligible boutique stock, to drive the Add to Bag / Back Soon / Out of Stock states on PDP and PLP. If MuleSoft cannot pre-aggregate, the storefront must decide whether to request both sources separately and aggregate client-side (extra round-trip) or fall back to SFCC-only inventory. This is distinct from the cart → checkout entry stock check (CAI-034) and the Find in Boutique flyout (CAI-038), both of which have their own endpoints. **Owner:** Integration team (Tryzens / MuleSoft).

## 4. Omneo

No Omneo-issued identifiers, hosts, or credentials are currently in Accenture's possession. All three items below are needed before implementation can begin against a real Omneo tenant; all three are hard blockers.

1. **Communication Preferences iFrame — confirm the non-Shopify auth handshake.** CRM-174 confirms the screen is rendered as an Omneo iFrame; the iFrame contains Communication Preferences, region/country selection (location, state, and language preference), and three clickable images that open the respective PLP within the iFrame (PLP-in-iFrame behaviour is an enhancement, not in scope for launch). Omneo documents embedding the Profile Portal as an iframe dialog — so the embed itself is a supported Omneo capability. However, Omneo's documented embed is a Shopify theme extension that authenticates via the Omneo CX Shopify app proxy, which a PWA does not have. Confirm, for the non-Shopify embed on Zimmermann's plan: the Profile Portal embed URL, how the Communication Preferences and region/country selection views are scoped within it, and the auth handshake outside Shopify (a customer-scoped signed-URL / HMAC approach, or a server-minted customer-scoped token). If no embed path is available, the fallback is a redirect to the hosted portal or a native rebuild against Omneo's API.
2. **Omneo identifiers and embed URL.** Provide the values needed to construct the iFrame `src` for production and each non-production environment:
   - Omneo tenant / account identifier (the value that appears in the embed URL, e.g. the account subdomain or path slug)
   - Exact embed URL host(s) and path(s) for the Communication Preferences widget — needed both to build the iFrame and to add to the storefront's `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` and `connect-src` allowlist
   - Any other public identifier the widget requires (widget ID, environment ID, configuration key)
3. **HMAC signing secret (or token mechanism).** Provide the per-environment secret/credential Omneo issues for the customer-scoped embed auth. Without it the Omneo ID proxy authentication cannot be exercised end-to-end; until it is provided, the integration can only be developed against a mock.

## 5. GiveX

1. **MuleSoft balance-check HTTPS contract.** The integration team to publish the request and response schema for the MuleSoft balance-check endpoint (`POST /givex/balance` placeholder) — the request carries both the card number and the PIN (secure PINs are enabled) — plus the error taxonomy that maps GiveX failure codes to the GC-042 / GC-060 / GC-061 customer-facing messages, including the invalid-PIN case. Without this contract the storefront cannot implement the call against a real MuleSoft instance. **Owner:** MuleSoft — GiveX supplies the underlying failure-code list; Zimmermann owns the final customer-facing message copy.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft endpoint, API token, and rate-limit thresholds.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: MuleSoft host, balance-check endpoint path, MuleSoft API token, and the agreed per-IP / per-session rate-limit thresholds and the bot-management vendor in front of the MRT route. **Owner:** MuleSoft (host / token / thresholds); the MRT-edge WAF / bot / rate-limit config is ours.
3. **Whether the balance-check route uses a CAPTCHA.** Confirm whether the MRT balance-check route should present a CAPTCHA challenge when the bot manager elevates a request — this is not yet decided. If a CAPTCHA is used, the simplest option is Google reCAPTCHA v3, reusing the site key already provisioned for register / login (no new provisioning). **Owner:** Zimmermann.

## 6. Booxi

Boutique appointment history is a PWA-direct read (PWA → MRT → Booxi); scope and timeline are TBC.

1. **Storefront scope and timeline (CRM-165 – CRM-167).** Confirm whether the My Account appointments surface is read-only history (current assumption) or whether in-storefront booking / rescheduling / cancellation is also in scope, and confirm the target sprint. Until confirmed, the section is built read-only and structured to slot in without redesign.
2. **Booxi API specification.** Booxi to publish the API contract for appointment history — endpoint(s), request and response schemas, the appointment status values and their customer-facing copy, error codes, and pagination. The PWA-side types are generated from this contract.
3. **Customer-identification mechanism (PWA-direct path).** Confirm how the storefront proves customer identity to Booxi without allowing the browser to retrieve an arbitrary customer's appointments — whether a Booxi customer ID is stored on the SFCC / Omneo profile (and how it is populated), or whether MRT must look the customer up in Booxi at request time. The mechanism must prevent impersonation.
4. **Per-environment Booxi credentials.** Booxi to supply, per environment: Booxi API host, API credential, and the credential rotation cadence and named owner. Note the API host is region-specific (e.g. a North America vs EU base URL), so confirm which regional host serves Zimmermann.

## 7. Adyen

1. **Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs.** Provide the Apple Pay and Google Pay merchant IDs per domain. Needed before the wallet buttons can be switched on. **Owner:** Zimmermann.
2. **Per-environment Adyen credentials.** Provide, for each environment (Dev / SIT / UAT / Stage / Prod — `Test` intentionally excluded here; it's a lightweight, on-demand pre-SIT tier expected to share Dev's sandbox credentials rather than provisioning its own. Revisit if that assumption turns out to be wrong.): client key, API key, HMAC key, merchant account ID per region, and whether it's a test or live Adyen account. Without these, checkout can't be tested against a real Adyen account.

## 8. Global-e

1. **Iframe embedding requirements.** Global-e to confirm and supply: (a) the `Content-Security-Policy` `frame-src` value for production and non-production Global-e checkout origins — needed to configure the storefront's security headers; and (b) the `postMessage` schema and trusted sender origin for iframe resize and order-completion signals — the PWA listener must verify `event.origin` against this value before acting. Neither can be guessed; both are needed before the iframe can be built.

2. **Order fields for international orders.** Confirm what order fields the PWA will receive for a Global-e order, to decide between rendering full order detail or a "View on tracking page" fallback. # Integration Open Items — Consolidated

> This is an aggregate of `.docs/integration` open items.

Open items requiring client confirmation across the fifteen external integrations in scope for the Zimmermann PWA storefront. Each item is a decision, contract, credential, or sign-off that must land before the corresponding integration can be implemented end-to-end against a real account.

## Summary

We need their documentations or implementation guide for at least:
Omneo iframe (for communication preferences), Booxi, MuleSoft (for GiveX balance check, order history/detail, returns).

Then for all the external systems (also incl. Adyen, Global-e, Google Maps, reCAPTCHA, Narvar, Didomi, GTM, Optimizely, Crazy Egg, Measmerize) we'll need their relevant Zimmermann-specific IDs, for each environment (dev/uat/prod etc) if applicable, and their associated Didomi feature/vendor ID if consent-gated.

Plus:

- GiveX: Do we need reCAPTCHA for balance check?
- CAI-023 Can MuleSoft aggregate stock?

| --- | ----------- | ---------------------- |
| 1   | SFCC        | 2                      |

## 1. SFCC

1. **Login MFA scope.** Confirm whether multi-factor authentication on login is in scope for launch or post-launch. If in scope, the SLAS configuration and the PWA login flow need additional design.

2. **`sfPayments.metadataUrl` hostname.** The `sfcc-payments` undici connection pool (TSD §12.1) assumes `config.app.sfPayments.metadataUrl` resolves to a different origin than the SCAPI host (`{shortCode}.api.commercecloud.salesforce.com`). If they share an origin the two pools should be merged.

## 2. Contentful

1. **`regions` content-model field.** The working assumption is that region-specific entries are filtered by a `regions` field containing the relevant SFCC site IDs. Pending content-strategy and editor-workflow sign-off — this field affects how editors author content across all eight storefronts.
2. **SFCC vs Contentful content ownership on composed pages.** The principle is settled — SFCC is the source of truth for all commerce data (product attributes, pricing, inventory, variations, gallery, category and search results) and Contentful owns standalone editorial (homepage, campaign landing pages, banners, lookbooks, size guides, footer). Not yet confirmed is the split on pages that compose both: which editorial blocks appear on the PDP and PLP and whether any are authored in SFCC Page Designer rather than Contentful, whether category landing pages are SFCC-routed or composed in Contentful Studio Experiences, and whether the mega-menu carries Contentful-authored promotional tiles alongside the SFCC category tree. Zimmermann and merchandising to confirm the per-surface split so the PDP, PLP, and navigation components can be built against a fixed data-source contract. The working assumption is captured in the content-ownership boundary table in the Contentful integration design (§1).
3. **Contentful Space and per-environment credentials.** Contentful to provision the Space and supply per-environment CDA token, CPA token, Space ID, environment ID, and webhook secret so the storefront can be exercised against a real Contentful environment.

## 3. MuleSoft

1. **MuleSoft OpenAPI specification.** MuleSoft to publish a versioned OpenAPI document covering every endpoint the storefront calls (order history and detail, returns, gift-card balance check, and any other MuleSoft-fronted endpoint in scope), including request and response schemas, error codes, and pagination contracts. The PDFs received (Jun 2025) provide sample schemas sufficient for initial implementation, but a formal versioned spec is still needed.
2. **Per-environment MuleSoft credentials.** MuleSoft to supply, per environment: `client_id`, `client_secret`, and MuleSoft host. Prod URLs for orders and returns are not yet provisioned (blank in the received PDFs). A staging Find In Store URL has been received (`https://mw.staging.zimmermann.com/magento-exp-api/api/find-in-store`); the production host is not yet confirmed.
3. **Response payload contracts for order detail and returns — mostly resolved.** Full sample schemas for order list, order detail, and returns were extracted from the Magento Experience Integration and Customer Order Transactions Sync PDFs (v3.0 / v2.0, Jun 2025) and are sufficient for initial implementation. === projectState In Progress + Unresolved ===
## In Progress
- **Header visual refinement**: layout and animations are implemented; still being iterated against the draft Figma to close remaining gaps

## What's Pending
- All integrations need to point to production accounts (SFCC, Contentful)
- Global-e integration (confirm pricing flow mechanism before implementing)
- Didomi consent management (implement per storefront defaults in REG-054)
- Omneo / Emarsys marketing sync
- Adyen payment integration
- MuleSoft middleware connections
- PDP, PLP, Cart, Checkout flows
- BOPIS (Collect in Boutique) checkout flow
- Full multi-site routing — 8 SFCC sites across 6 regions (AU, US domestic, US international, UK, EU domestic, EU international, HK, ME). **US site topology updated (REG-005, 2026-07-10):** US splits into two separate SFCC sites — US domestic (`/us/`, SFCC checkout) and US international (`/en-ca/`, Global-e checkout). New site ID `ZimmermannUSIntl` pending BM confirmation.
- Address autocomplete via Google Maps API
- Narvar EDD + tracking integration
- SEO: hreflang, canonical URLs, sitemaps
- Order-on-behalf (OOBO) for CS agents
- Retail Rewards (AP21) integration
- Gift card PDP, cart, checkout, and GiveX integration
- Promotions engine and multi-currency/FX pricebook setup
- CI workflow split — two complementary workflows, each with a clear role:
  - `qa.yml` (every PR to `develop`/`release/**`): `unit-tests` (Vitest) + `storybook-test` (Storybook `play` + `@storybook/addon-a11y`, `storybook test --ci`) run in parallel; `e2e-browserstack` on release PRs only. **`storybook-test` job is wired but pending `@storybook/addon-test` and `@storybook/addon-a11y` installation (feature/storybook-v10 upgrade task).**
  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:
- Product copy ownership: Contentful vs SFCC vs AP21 (TBD).
- Translation trigger workflow with TransPerfect (TBD).
- Global-e + Didomi consent interaction (TBD).
- **Social login (Apple/Google):** Confirmed in scope for launch (ENH-004, Must-Have, Go-Live) as SFCC OOTB configuration only. **Hard dependency:** Apple and Google merchant accounts must be provisioned by Zimmermann before implementation can start. Do not implement until merchant accounts exist.
- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.
- **Denmark routing:** Which storefront Denmark resolves to is not yet confirmed.
- **EU billing fields:** Locale-specific billing fields (Italian Codice Fiscale, Spanish NIF, French SIRET) — to be confirmed before implementing.
- **Adyen dynamic checkout (ENH-020):** Confirmed Must-Have for Go-Live, but a **hard dependency on Adyen** delivering A/B-able dynamic payment-method display. Do not assume the feature is buildable end-to-end until Adyen delivery is confirmed.
- **Optimizely SFCC data-layer scope (AAB-004):** Load mechanism Confirmed (PWA-direct head tag, US-only, Zimmermann-provided script). Residual: Tell No Lies suspects no SFCC-side data-layer work is needed for Optimizely (Magento launch was GTM-only). Confirm with Tell No Lies before doing SFCC data-layer work specifically for Optimizely.
- **CRM-155 customer group precedence:** Rules for resolving overlapping customer group memberships are TBD.
- **Mulesoft stock aggregation (CAI-023):** Confirmation pending that Mulesoft can aggregate warehouse + boutique stock pre-checkout.
- **Search/recommendation platform:** SFCC Einstein is confirmed on the Search sheet (SPR-63). **Cross-sheet contradiction (flag, do not resolve):** the Cart & Inventory sheet CAI-005 now states "search / recommendation engine not confirmed" with RJ noting "99% likely we will move away from Athos" — i.e. the engine is being treated as open there. Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.
- **PRC-45 Retail Rewards count per order:** Requirement text says "maximum of one Retail Reward per order" but RJ challenges: "Multiple retail rewards can be applied per order." Downgraded to Open — confirm the cap before building reward-application logic.
- **Addingwell role in analytics (AAB-001/003):** AAB-001 frames all container/tag logic as living in GTM (Tell No Lies), while the Third Party Integrations rows say the GTM container loads *via the Addingwell MRT integration* and GA4/downstream tags route through an Addingwell *server-side container*. Reconciled in analytics.md as logic-vs-transport, but confirm with Tell No Lies whether Addingwell is none / transport-only / server-side routing.
- **DMU-007 order history source (upstream):** DMU-007 PWA contract Confirmed (displays MuleSoft payload). Residual upstream conflict: requirement + JT say NewStore via MuleSoft; RJ says "Order history will come from Omneo." Out of PWA boundary — reconcile so the integration contract is unambiguous.
- **DMU-009 Contentful setup ownership:** RJ: "This is no longer required as AS will be setting up Contentful." Downgraded pending reconciliation of who owns CMS setup.
- **Customer migration shape (DMU-004):** Only email + Omneo ID migrated; name, phone, addresses, comms prefs sourced **live from Omneo at login**. My Account profile pages must round-trip to Omneo post-auth. Graceful degradation for Omneo outages on account screens is now load-bearing — confirm UX before implementing profile reads.
- **Asset/CDN migration & platform (DMU-010 / DMU-020):** Asset migration de-scoped — no asset 301s; images stay in Contentful. Separately, the source note now records the platform CDN as Akamai (SFCC default), which sits against existing Cloudflare carry-forward references — confirm the CDN platform of record (no asset-migration impact either way).
- **PRC-43 Global-e cartridge customer-group catalogue prices:** Open with Global-e — does the cartridge honour customer-group catalogue prices (VIC) at international checkout? Also: how do VIC customers currently receive discounts at Global-e checkout in M2? Do not assume VIC pricing flows through Global-e until confirmed.
- **CFD-070 guest account creation flow:** Dependent on the guest journey design — open.
- **CFD-045 BOPIS seeding mechanism:** Open — how Collect in Boutique availability is seeded into checkout still TBC.
- **PAY-022 Adyen CVC config:** Confirm CVC-on-saved-card configuration with Adyen. PWA behaviour (re-entry required) is Confirmed.
- **PAY-047/048/049 fraud hold scope:** Adyen/NewStore-owned per IC; PWA-side display behaviour not yet signed off.
- **OM-002 MuleSoft order export gating:** Sign-off pending on the exact attribute set passed at order export.
- **OM-017/018 NewStore order status taxonomy:** SFCC displays raw MuleSoft status; mapping list still open.
- **OM-034 back-in-stock FIFO email logic:** Sign-off pending.
- **DLV-012 free-shipping thresholds:** Per-delivery-method per-storefront rate card updated; re-sign-off pending.

  - `digital-sit.yml` (push/PR to `release/**`): four parallel jobs into `sit-gate` — `playwright-p0` (Chromium P0 suite), `bundle-size` (bundlewatch, main.js < 180 kB / vendor.js < 250 kB / main.css < 50 kB), `contract-tests` (placeholder; real MuleSoft OpenAPI assertion pending spec source), `lighthouse-ci` (Perf ≥ 80, A11y ≥ 90, Best Practices ≥ 90; requires LHCI server secrets)
- **`e2e-localhost` (qa.yml) is fixed and re-enabled, as of PR #35 (`bugfix/ci-e2e-test`, merged 2026-07-16).** Root cause of the "homepage smoke test fails in CI, logo never found" issue (open as of PR #30): `BasePage.js`'s old `dismissConsent()` wrapped both `waitFor()` and `.click()` in one `try/catch`, so a real click failure was silently swallowed as "no dialog appeared" — if a consent dialog genuinely appeared in CI (injected by something outside this repo's own source, e.g. GTM/MRT platform config — not by anything grep-visible in `overrides/`) and the click failed transiently, the `aria-modal` dialog stayed open and blocked the entire page's accessibility tree, exactly matching the symptom. Fixed by CodeRabbit-prompted review in PR #30 (separated `.click()` out of the `try/catch`) — but that fix was never actually exercised in CI until PR #35 re-enabled the job, confirmed via 4 consecutive clean CI passes. Along the way also: added an HTML reporter to `playwright.config.js` (every project except `p0` had been silently producing an empty `playwright-report/` — CI failures were undebuggable from artifacts alone); fixed a webpack-build-race (`wait-on` only confirms the port is open, not that the client bundle finished compiling — added a step polling `dev-server.log` for `webpack built client`); fixed the original missing-Commerce-API-env-vars bug (job now binds `environment: dev`, sources `COMMERCE_API_*` from `vars.*`, `scripts/switchEnv.mjs`'s `push <tier>` uploads a shared+tier merge so one environment binding is self-sufficient); switched the job gate from `always()` to `!cancelled()` so a superseded/cancelled run doesn't burn a 15-min runner slot.
- PR #30 (`feature/gh-qa-workflow`, merged) also: deleted the unfinished `SFCC-000_guest-checkout` placeholder (never had real Adyen payment interaction, self-described `EXAMPLE` in its own header) and its `testIgnore` mis-scoping (ran under `chromium`/`mobile-chrome` `retries:2` instead of the dedicated `p0` project's `retries:0`, costing ~12 of the ~14 min `e2e-localhost` runtime on every PR); added a homepage smoke test (new `homepage` E2E area + `SMOKE-` naming convention for Jira-less tests); fixed a `@typescript-eslint/no-var-requires` misconfiguration flagging `require()` in `e2e/`'s intentionally-CommonJS files; added `test-results/`/`playwright-report/` to `.gitignore`.
- **Proposed: tag-based environment promotion (GitFlow) — full spec on Confluence, implementation not yet started.** Full rationale, tag naming convention, worked commands, and open questions:
  [Proposed: Tag-Based Environment Promotion (GitFlow)](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/335216656/Proposed+Tag-Based+Environment+Promotion+GitFlow)
  (Confluence, v5, child of the Branching Guide page). Summary: only `Dev` should be continuously tied to `develop`; every other tier should deploy a specific, immutable git tag (`vX.Y.Z-rc.N` / `vX.Y.Z` / `vX.Y.Z-hotfix.N`, cut via `npm version`) instead of a branch ref, so Test/SIT/UAT/Stage can each run independent testing cycles instead of being forced onto the same moving branch. **Do not implement the AGENTS.md/governance pieces without squad-lead + Integration-lead sign-off — this is still a proposal.** Implementation checklist for a fresh session on a new branch (see the Confluence page for full detail on each item):
  - **Decided 2026-07-16** (see Confluence page's "Decisions made so far" table): release cadence is per-sprint; pre-launch versioning starts at `v0.1.0` (MAJOR locked at `0` until go-live, which becomes `v1.0.0`); `Test` gets its own automated CI gate (not manual-only); tag protection + the version-guard + Release-per-final-tag are all adopted immediately, not phased in.
  - **Tooling — safe to build now, doesn't touch governance docs:**
    1. `npm version` adoption — no code change needed, it's a built-in npm command; just start using it per the Confluence page's "How to deploy" section instead of raw `git tag`. First tag will be `v0.1.0-rc.0`.
    2. **Primary enforcement — one GitHub Ruleset covers both naming and immutability:** Settings → Rules → Rulesets → New tag ruleset, targeting `v*`, with a "tag name pattern" rule requiring `^v\d+\.\d+\.\d+(-rc\.\d+|-hotfix\.\d+)?$` plus "restrict creation," "restrict updates," and "restrict deletion" all enabled. This genuinely hard-blocks a non-matching tag at push time *and* prevents force-push/delete on matching tags — all on GitHub.com, not Enterprise Server-only (corrected from an earlier draft of this note, which wrongly split this into a separate "tag protection rules" step and claimed pattern-blocking wasn't possible on GitHub.com). Keep a `push: tags: ['*']` validation workflow too, as defense-in-depth / for a clearer failure message than the raw ruleset rejection gives.
    3. A version-guard step added to each `deploy-*.yml` (test/sit/stg/uat/prod) — fetch the environment's current deployed tag via `gh api repos/ZimmermannAU/zimmermann-pwa/deployments?environment=<env>`, semver-compare against the tag being deployed (use the `semver` npm package, not hand-rolled bash comparison — pre-release identifiers must be dot-separated, e.g. `-rc.10` vs `-rc.2`, or numeric comparison breaks), fail on a downgrade. **`<env>` must be the actual GitHub Environment name, not the workflow-file suffix** — they diverge for `stg` (`deploy-stg.yml` targets the `staging` Environment, not `stg`; we hit this exact mismatch once already this session, commit `12bf91b`). Map each tier explicitly (`stg` → `staging`, everything else matches its filename) rather than deriving it from the filename. Fail closed if the environment name is wrong or the API call errors — a genuine first-ever deployment (no prior Deployment record at all) is fine to proceed, but an unresolvable environment/API error is not the same thing and must not be treated as "nothing to compare against, allow it."
    4. **A Test-tier CI gate** — new, decided 2026-07-16. Proposed shape (not yet confirmed, see the page's remaining two open questions): a second job appended to `deploy-test.yml` that runs a P0-only Playwright suite against whatever was just deployed, so the run's pass/fail becomes the "safe to promote to SIT" signal — deliberately deploy-then-gate rather than SIT Gate's gate-then-deploy, since `Test` is on-demand (`workflow_dispatch`, including raw feature branches) and has no push/PR event to hang a pre-check on.
    5. Wire `/generate-changelog`'s existing `gh release create` offer into the "cut the final tag" step — no new tooling, the skill already does this.
  - **Governance — needs squad-lead + Integration-lead review before merging:**
    6. A new `.claude/rules/tagging.md` (or fold into `.docs/releaseBranchesRules.md`, already auto-loaded on `release/*`/`hotfix/*`) documenting the tag convention and instructing Claude to always use `npm version`, never hand-construct a tag string.
    7. `AGENTS.md`'s branch table / the Confluence Branching Guide itself, once the team has actually reviewed and approved the proposal — this repo's `AGENTS.md` requires both squad leads and the Integration lead to sign off on changes to itself, stronger than the usual verified-session Tier 1 exception.
  - Still open per the Confluence page: exact Test-gate design (deploy-then-gate as proposed, or match SIT's gate-then-deploy exactly) and its scope (P0 suite only, or also bundle-size/contract-tests/Lighthouse).

## Unresolved Dependencies
Do not hard-code assumptions for the following — ask the user before implementing:

- **Omneo guest record creation timing:** When to create an Omneo record for a guest (at newsletter sign-up, at back-in-stock capture, at checkout, or only at order completion) is under legal/SFCC best-practice review. SFCC best practice is order completion only. Do not create Omneo records for guests at any earlier point until confirmed. Note: CRM-012–015 are signed off but Tony Tilbrook (early creation) and Izzy Coxon (order-completion only) currently disagree on the timing — treat as Open until reconciled.

Confirm which sheet is authoritative before relying on Einstein for cart/recommendation surfaces.

Here is the audit. --- # PART 1 — CONFORMANCE ## 1.0 The gate-set discrepancy (report first, as instructed) The two documents specify **different** pre-PR gate sets. | Source | Gates | |---|---| | Playbook, Play 5 "Gate zero" (lines 360-364) | `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run lint` · `npx vitest run` — **3** | | Manual §8 (lines 875-881, 909-917) | `npx tsc --noEmit` · `npm run lint` · `npm test` · `npm run build-storybook && npx test-storybook` · `/code-quality` · **plus** `coderabbit auth status && cr review --light --base develop` ("**required, not optional**") — **6** | The manual is the fuller set and is the one I audited against. The gap is material, not cosmetic: the manual itself explains why (§8 line 883) — *"**Vitest does not run `play` functions.** A change that breaks a story passes `npm test` and fails in CI. That happened on the footer PR."* A developer following the playbook's gate zero on this very branch would have shipped that failure. **The playbook's Play 5 needs the Storybook gate added.** ## 1.1 Gate results on this branch | # | Gate | Verdict | Evidence | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `npx tsc --noEmit` clean | **PASS** | exit 0, no output | | 2 | `npm run lint` "must not add new errors" | **PASS** | 19 errors, **all** in `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/definitions.ts` (17) and `overrides/app/routes.tsx` (2); `git diff origin/develop --name-only` returns **0** for both. All 19 are auto-fixable `prettier/prettier`. The 3 `header/index.tsx` warnings are pre-existing (branch diff there is comments only). | | 3 | `npm test` (Vitest) | **PASS** | 8 files, **185/185** passed | | 4 | `build-storybook && test-storybook` | **CANNOT-VERIFY** | Excluded by your instruction. PR body claims it ran. | | 5 | `/code-quality` | **PASS (inferred)** | commit `98dc464 fix(ui-kit): code quality fixes — spelling, type imports, and inline cast comments` | | 6 | `cr review --light --base develop` | **PASS (claimed)** | PR body: "Local CodeRabbit — no new findings"; commits `8aec89b`, `5b33f84` address CodeRabbit findings | **Two PR-body claims are stale/inaccurate** (worth correcting, since the manual makes the PR the record of the gate): - "`npm run lint` — **0 errors**" — repo-wide it is 19. Accurate as *"no new errors"*, not as stated. - "Vitest — **168/168**" (actual 185) and "**15** `play` functions across 7 stories" (actual **19**, `grep -c "play:"`). --- ## 1.2 Copy-first — **FAIL** Manual §2 (lines 232-245) names the file explicitly: > *"`product-tile`, `display-price`, `swatch-group`, `image-gallery`, `link`, **`footer`**, `list-menu`, `drawer-menu` and `seo` are all still **`Origin = Base`**"* … *"**Most stories you pick up will pay copy-first.**"* Manual §2 (lines 248-256) / Playbook Play 1 (lines 145-153) require: copy base file → convert to TS → `tsc` → **temporary `console.log` marker** → **stop, human confirms the override renders** → then build, remove markers. Evidence this did not happen: - The base file exists: `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/components/footer/index.jsx` - The **first** commit touching `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx` is `8c25f11` *"feat(footer): SFCC-55 global footer UI"* — and that first version is already a bespoke Zimmermann rewrite (imports `ZimmLogo`/`ZimmIcon`/`ZimmNavItem`/`FOOTER_FIXTURE`), not a port of the base. - `git log origin/develop..HEAD -S "[overrides]"` → **zero commits**. No marker was ever added or removed. - No separate scaffold commit exists; the copy-first stage was never a distinct, human-gated step. This is the item the manual calls out at §11 as mistake **#8** — *"Skipping copy-first on an `Origin = Base` component."* **Mitigating fact, stated fairly:** the *end state* is correct — the override does intercept (base `_app/index.jsx:43` imports footer by package path; `_app/index.jsx:484` renders `
`), and the registry now records `Footer | Override | ... | 14` consumers. The process gate was skipped, not the outcome. ## 1.3 The bridge pattern — **FAIL** (low real risk) Manual §4 Step 2 (lines 689-699): > *"Any hits mean base components depend on it, so its **default export must stay a faithful, undecorated port** — full original prop surface, same `forwardRef` behaviour. Put Zimmermann-only styling behind a **named export** that wraps the default."* The grep the manual prescribes returns a hit (`_app/index.jsx:43`). The override inverts the prescribed split: `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:416` is `export const Footer` (presentational) and `:560` is `export default FooterContainer` — a **new** prop surface (`data`, `copyrightYear`, `initialSubscribed`, `enableNameCapture`, `onLogoClick`, `privacyPolicyHref`), not the base's. Real risk is near-nil: base renders `
` with **no props**, and checkout uses a separate `CheckoutFooter`. But the documented rule is unmet, and the manual's own escape hatch was not used — §4 line 704-708: *"you may well be the one who establishes the first example of it. **If you are, say so in the PR** so the rule file can be updated."* The PR does not say so. ## 1.4 "Minimal changes" / base capability removed — **FAIL (partially annotated)** Manual §4 Step 2: *"**Minimal changes** — don't remove base functionality you weren't asked to touch."* Because the override intercepts site-wide, the base footer's locale ``, `LinksList`, `SubscribeMarketingConsent`, `LocaleText` and store-locator link are gone from every page. The concrete regression is annotated in-code at `overrides/app/components/footer/index.tsx:33-36`: ``` const LOCALE_LABEL_PLACEHOLDER = 'Australia (AUD) / ENG'; ``` > *"…it previously read "United States (USD) / ENG" on an AU storefront. The real fix reads site.l10n.defaultLocale and the site's currency via useMultiSite when the locale selector lands"* So a working locale switcher became a hardcoded, non-functional label. **Credit where due:** it is flagged in-code with the correct fix named — that is exactly "raise, don't invent". **But it is not disclosed in the PR body**, and the manual makes the PR the place a design/scope gap gets surfaced (§8 line 906-907). ## 1.5 The ladder — **FAIL on recording** Manual §4 Step 1 (line 675): *"Report what you found in the PR description, **even when the answer is "nothing"** — that's the evidence the ladder was walked."* §4 Step 2: *"**Build custom** … Justify the call in the PR."* §8 self-check: *"[ ] Ladder walked — reuse checked and reported, 'custom' justified."* PR #59's body has no ladder statement, no registry/`Origin` finding, and no justification for building rather than extending. It justifies *adjacent* decisions well (the `ZimmFooter` recipe key, the chevron replacement) but never the rung. Playbook Play 5 review question 2 — *"Is it an override, or a bespoke build — and if bespoke, why?"* — is unanswerable from the PR. ## 1.6 Component governance — a second Button — **FAIL** This is the highest-value finding, and it is exactly the one the playbook says no tool will catch (Play 5, line 348: *"**Duplication / reuse** — No tool detects 'this is a second Button'. This is the core of responsibility #3 and it is entirely human"*). Two Zimmermann buttons now exist, both thin mapping layers over Chakra `
